title: Completed frame torsor monodromy restricts to the generic cocycle
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Write $k=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ for its function field, choose a separable closure $k^s/k$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and put $G_k=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its profinite Krull topology. For any nonarchimedean normed field $A$ (a field with a multiplicative absolute value satisfying $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$), put $R_{A,T}=p_T^*\underline A$, where $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ for profinite $S$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. All module objects and lisse modules are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use all continuous functions with the norm topology. Assume further that $X$ is quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. Let $\bar\eta$ be the geometric generic point given by an algebraic closure containing $k^s$, and let $q:G_k\to\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar\eta)$ be induced by the generic point $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Put $F=\widehat A$, with canonical isometric inclusion $\iota:A\hookrightarrow F$ [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. Let $L$ be a lisse $R_{A,X}$-module of constant finite rank $n\geq0$, and choose a basis of $V_A(L)=\Gamma((\operatorname{Spec}k^s)_{\mathrm{proet}},L|_{k^s})$. Write $\sigma_L:G_k\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ for its descent cocycle in that basis, with the convention of [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates]. Form
$$L_F=R_{F,X}\otimes_{R_{A,X}}L$$
by ordinary internal scalar extension along postcomposition by $\iota$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Then $L_F$ is lisse of rank $n$, and its frame sheaf $P(U)=\operatorname{Isom}_{R_{F,U}}(R_{F,U}^n,L_F|_U)$ is a right $F_{\operatorname{GL}_n(F)}$-torsor [def-sfb-continuous-right-torsor], with action by precomposition and $F_G(U)=C(|U|,G)$; here $\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$, with the topology from $F^{n\times n}$, is a Hausdorff group with an open-subgroup identity basis, complete for its two-sided uniformity [lem-sfb-complete-nonarchimedean-matrix-group], so it satisfies the coefficient-group hypotheses of [lem-sfb-complete-group-torsor-monodromy]. The chosen basis induces a point $p$ of its geometric generic fibre. Let $\tau_L:\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar\eta)\to\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ be the homomorphism assigned to $(P,p)$ by [lem-sfb-complete-group-torsor-monodromy]. Then
$$\tau_L(q(g))=\iota_*\sigma_L(g)\quad(g\in G_k),$$
where $\iota_*$ applies $\iota$ to every matrix entry. In particular the restriction of the pointed completed frame torsor to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has precisely the embedded generic cocycle, with this convention and without an inversion. The cocycle $\sigma_L$ is trivial on $\ker q$ and has a unique factor $\rho_L:\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar\eta)\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ satisfying $\sigma_L=\rho_Lq$; this factor is continuous. For two modules, a linear map between their generic vector spaces intertwines their generic cocycles if and only if it intertwines these factored representations.

source.place: Agent coefficient-completion/frame comparison in the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71; uses the field clause of the separately recorded complete-group torsor correspondence.

proof.text: The completion lemma gives an injective isometric continuous field map $\iota:A\to F$. The matrix-group lemma gives the nonarchimedean inequality on $F$ and all three required properties of $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$: Hausdorffness, an open-subgroup identity basis and two-sided completeness, including $n=0$. Both fields are totally disconnected: if $a\ne b$, a ball of radius less than $|a-b|$ containing $a$ is clopen and excludes $b$; its complement is open by the ultrametric inequality. Since an integral scheme is irreducible, $X$ is connected. Its quasi-compactness and local Noetherianness give exactly the base hypotheses of the torsor correspondence.

source.place: Agent assembly of completion and matrix-group inputs, in the framework of Proposition 7.1.5 and Lemma 7.4.7.

proof.text: Apply the generic scalar-comparison lemma with $B=F$ and $\varphi=\iota$. It gives lisseness of $L_F$ with rank $n$, identifies its generic vector space with $F\otimes_A V_A(L)$, and identifies its generic descent matrices with $\iota_*\sigma_L$. Thus the chosen basis extends to a basis over $F$. The lemma applies to arbitrary nonarchimedean normed fields and continuous coefficient inclusions, so it requires neither local compactness nor completeness of $A$.

source.place: Agent coefficient-completion specialization of the entrywise tensor comparison; Lemma 7.4.7 framework.

proof.text: Use the canonical continuous-function realization of $R_{F,X}$, applicable because $F$ is totally disconnected. On a slice where $L_F$ has a frame $e$, any other frame is uniquely $e\circ h$, with $h$ an invertible matrix over $R_F(U)=C(|U|,F)$. Such matrices are exactly $C(|U|,G)$: the entries give a continuous map into the subspace $G\subset F^{n\times n}$, and conversely a continuous $G$-valued map and its continuous inverse give inverse matrices over $C(|U|,F)$. The maps $h\mapsto e\circ h$ commute with restriction, and $(e\circ h)\circ h'=e\circ(hh')$. Hence the frame sheaf is locally the regular right $F_G$-sheaf and satisfies the right-torsor definition. This also proves that geometric restriction identifies it with the frame sheaf of the restricted module: in each such chart both restrictions are $h\mapsto e|\circ h$, and these identifications agree on overlaps.

source.place: Example 3.1, p. 6; elementary matrix description of the frame sheaf and its restriction.

proof.text: Over $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ the extended basis is a frame $p$. Write $e$ for the original $A$-basis frame. In the Cech coordinates and convention of the field lemma, $\mathrm{pr}_2^*e=\mathrm{pr}_1^*e\circ c_L$ and $c_L(g)=\sigma_L(g)$. Scalar extension is entrywise postcomposition on these Cech rings and free modules. Therefore $\mathrm{pr}_2^*p=\mathrm{pr}_1^*p\circ\iota_*(c_L)$, so the right frame-torsor cocycle is $g\mapsto\iota_*\sigma_L(g)$. The right action is precomposition, precisely the composition just displayed: no inverse matrix occurs. The fibre identification in the field clause of the torsor correspondence transports this frame to the asserted geometric generic point.

source.place: Agent Cech-coordinate computation with the field clause of the pointed torsor correspondence; Lemma 7.4.7 framework.

proof.text: Apply the pointed torsor correspondence to $(P,p)$ on $X$. All its hypotheses were checked in Step 1, and Step 3 supplies its torsor input. Its pullback naturality along the pointed generic morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ says that the pullback has representation $\tau_L\circ q$. The field clause says that this representation is its right descent cocycle in the point $p$. Step 4 computed that cocycle, giving $\tau_L(q(g))=\iota_*\sigma_L(g)$ for every $g\in G_k$.

source.place: Pullback naturality and the field clause of the separately recorded complete-group torsor correspondence; Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10 framework.

proof.text: The normal integral Galois-presentation lemma gives continuity and surjectivity of $q$. If $g\in\ker q$, Step 5 gives $\iota_*\sigma_L(g)=I$; entrywise injectivity of $\iota$ gives $\sigma_L(g)=I$. For $h\in\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar\eta)$ choose $g$ with $q(g)=h$ and define $\rho_L(h)=\sigma_L(g)$. Two choices differ by an element of $\ker q$, so this is well-defined. Lifting two elements and multiplying their lifts proves multiplicativity; lifting one proves $\sigma_L=\rho_Lq$. Surjectivity proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia, clause (1); elementary kernel factorization.

proof.text: The matrix inclusion $\iota_*:\operatorname{GL}_n(A)\to\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ is a topological embedding: on the ambient finite matrix products this follows coordinatewise from the isometry $\iota$, and both general linear groups have the subspace topology. Step 5 therefore makes $\sigma_L$ continuous, since $\tau_Lq$ is continuous and takes values in that embedded subgroup. The source of $q$ is profinite and its target is Hausdorff, so the compact-Hausdorff quotient lemma makes $q$ a quotient map. For every open $W\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$, $q^{-1}(\rho_L^{-1}W)=\sigma_L^{-1}W$ is open, whence $\rho_L^{-1}W$ is open. Finally, for any two modules and any linear map $T$, the equations $T\sigma_L(g)=\sigma_M(g)T$ for all $g$ become exactly $T\rho_L(h)=\rho_M(h)T$ for all $h$, by surjectivity of $q$. For $n=0$ the frame and matrix group are singletons, the kernel computation and continuity are automatic, and the same equations handle rectangular matrices with an empty dimension.
